newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine share index soars 7.23 pct in midtrade.
newsitem.headline: Philippine share index soars 7.23 pct in midtrade.

text.p: The Philippine composite index gained 181.57 points, or 7.23 percent, to 2,692.72 points in midsession as the market reacted positively to the Central Bank's decision allowing the peso to fall, traders said.

"The whole pattern has been reversed and the public is back into equities. Unexpectedly, the market went boom. This just goes to show you that the market is not dead," said Irving Ackerman, president at I. Ackerman & Co Inc.
Turnover was heavy at 1.82 billion pesos with 85 gainers to five losers.
"The Central Bank's decision just loosened the pressure off the stock market," said Jose Ricardo Garcia, executive vice-president at Diversified Securities.
Firstliner issues were carrying the market to new heights in midsession, led by San Miguel Corp B, Metrobank, Ayala Land Inc B, Meralco B and PLDT.

PLDT reached an intra-day high of 935 pesos, gaining 85 pesos in mid-trade. Traders said the issue is seen to benefit from a weakening of the peso as it sources 50 percent of its revenues from international calls.
